title: The Missing Refund
brief: Marcus Bell returned a $312 jacket to Northwind Outfitters. Three weeks later — no refund, and the store says it never got the package. Marcus wants the bureau to force Northwind to pay. Find out where the jacket went before you stamp the respondent.

claim.statement: Northwind Outfitters refuses to refund $312 for a jacket I returned on October 2. I followed their support's instructions exactly. Make them pay.

documents.title: Domain lookup — northwind-returnshelp.example

body.heading: Domain registration lookup
body.body:
Domain: northwind-returnshelp.example. Created: 09/12/2026. Registrar: CheapNames Inc. Registrant: privacy protected in the public lookup. Registrant phone: (937) 555-0142. Note: the official Northwind Outfitters domain is northwindoutfitters.example (created 2011).

Dispute supplement, 10/21/2026: the registrar’s verified abuse response identifies the domain account administrator and fee beneficiary as Kyle Denton. Preserved support records show that this account sent Marcus the label for order NW-58213, tracking PG-77310452, directed the jacket to 880 Industrial Way, Unit 12, and collected the $4.99 label fee for the same operator. It presented itself as Northwind Returns Support. Northwind’s verified response confirms that this site and its operator are not affiliated with or authorized by Northwind, which has received neither this return request nor the jacket. This supplement identifies the operator; a shared phone number alone would not prove who sent the label.

methods.text: Northwind received the jacket and is stalling the refund.
A neighbor stole the package from the hallway before it was shipped.
A fake 'Northwind support' site sent Marcus a label to the scammer's own warehouse.
ParcelGo lost the package in transit.

solution.explanation: Northwind Outfitters is NOT GUILTY: the retailer never received or authorized this return, although Marcus was a victim of a separate scam. The domain dispute record identifies Kyle Denton as the administrator who sent the fake Northwind label, and the company filing proves that Kyle owns QuickShip Returns LLC at the destination address. ParcelGo independently confirms delivery there, signed by K. DENTON, so neither a hallway theft nor a lost parcel explains this shipment. The official help page shows that real Northwind labels are free and go to Fairview; Kyle’s lookalike site charged $4.99 and sent the jacket to his own warehouse. Marcus can still contact the real Northwind support before 10/24/2026 and report the impersonation.
